articles.title: The PHP2Shell Postmortem: What CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 Actually Tell Us
articles.excerpt: I made a 6-minute video breakdown of this on YouTube — this is the written version for readers who prefer text. Same facts, same angles, better for linking in Slack or coming back to later. On October…
articles.body: I made a 6-minute video breakdown of this on YouTube — this is the written version for readers who prefer text. Same facts, same angles, better for linking in Slack or coming back to later. On October 17, 2026 — four days before the patch shipped — AWS's MadPot honeypot caught something unusual: one HTTP request, no login, no session, no account. The server came back wrong. Three days later, the CVE numbers for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 leaked on Hacker News, roughly 22 hours before the planned embargo lift. By the time PHP 8.5.12 / 8.4.27 / 8.3.36 / 8.2.35 went out, the exploit was already in the wild. This post walks through four things I think are worth sitting with: the attack shape, the attacker fingerprint, the leak chain, and the 22-year pattern underneath.

articles.body: Python scripts are a powerful tool for automating tasks and building applications quickly. However, that convenience can also open doors to vulnerabilities if good security practices are not followed. Below we describe the five most frequent mistakes that appear in real‑world projects and offer practical recommendations to mitigate them. 1. Poor Exception Handling Inadequate exception handling allows unexpected errors to leak to the user or cause the application to crash abruptly, exposing sensitive information such as system paths or stack traces. According to the article “Script Python revela errores de seguridad críticos” [^1], poor exception handling is one of the most common vulnerabilities.

articles.title: Cisco ISE CVE-2026-20241 turns certificate issuance into an authorization decision
articles.excerpt: Cisco ISE CVE-2026-20241 turns certificate issuance into an authorization decision Cisco published an authorization bypass in Identity Services Engine and the Passive Identity Connector on November 4,…
articles.body: Cisco ISE CVE-2026-20241 turns certificate issuance into an authorization decision Cisco published an authorization bypass in Identity Services Engine and the Passive Identity Connector on November 4, 2026. The advisory assigns CVE-2026-20241 a CVSS base score of 5.3 and says an unauthenticated, remote attacker can obtain an endpoint identity certificate. That description is short, but the operational consequence is larger than the certificate itself. ISE issues and validates credentials that network policy uses to decide whether an endpoint belongs on a network. The advisory does not expose the vulnerable code path. It also lists no workarounds. Administrators should therefore avoid filling the gap with assumptions about the exact request or target API.

articles.body: You've built an AI application that works perfectly on your local RTX 4090. Now you need to deploy it — and you discover that the major cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure) charge enterprise prices for GPU instances that would bankrupt your indie SaaS before it gets its first paying customer. Enter the GPU cloud specialists: RunPod, Vast.ai, and Lambda Labs, all of which offer significantly cheaper GPU compute by leveraging spot pricing, community-owned hardware, or specialized infrastructure. But which one actually works for production AI inference? Quick Verdict 🏆 RunPod is the best overall choice for indie developers deploying AI inference — it offers the most reliable serverless GPU experience with excellent tooling and reasonable pricing.

articles.excerpt: Three AI code reviewers, one file. That shift happened faster than most teams noticed. AGENTS.md was formalized in August 2025 as a shared config format co-promoted by OpenAI, Google, Sourcegraph, Cur…
articles.body: Three AI code reviewers, one file. That shift happened faster than most teams noticed. AGENTS.md was formalized in August 2025 as a shared config format co-promoted by OpenAI, Google, Sourcegraph, Cursor, Factory, and others. By September 2026, Claude Code v2.1.277 shipped native AGENTS.md support — if no CLAUDE.md is present, Claude Code falls back to AGENTS.md. GitHub Copilot CLI reads it. Cursor reads it. The spec at agents.md is now the closest thing to a universal standard for AI coding agents. If one file configures three review tools, the question becomes: what should actually be in it for code review? Why "review" belongs in AGENTS.md, not in a separate .review.md The temptation is to split.

articles.body: Two spacewalking astronauts will finish upgrading the International Space Station's power system today (Nov. 5), and you can watch the action live. NASA astronaut Anil Menon and the Canadian Space Agency 's Joshua Kutryk will install the eighth and final International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Array (iROSA) today, during a roughly seven-hour spacewalk that's scheduled to begin at 8:30 a.m. EST (1330 GMT). You can watch it live here at Space.com , courtesy of NASA, beginning at 7 a.m. EDT (1200 GMT). NASA astronaut Anil Menon points his camera toward his spacesuit’s helmet visor and takes a selfie during a spacewalk on Oct. 29, 2026.

articles.title: Zyxel GS1900 Patch Fails to Block Zero-Day Exploit Allowing Root Command Execution
articles.excerpt: Zyxel GS1900 network switches that received the vendor's earlier fix for an actively exploited flaw are still open to the exploit attackers used, researchers at Binarly found. The exploit lets anyone…
articles.body: Zyxel GS1900 network switches that received the vendor's earlier fix for an actively exploited flaw are still open to the exploit attackers used, researchers at Binarly found. The exploit lets anyone who can reach a switch's web management interface run commands on it without logging in. Zyxel has released new firmware for 10 GS1900 models that closes the hole. articles.body: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 5 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Enceladus in Silhouette Explanation: One of our Solar System’s most tantalizing worlds, Enceladus is backlit by the Sun in this Cassini spacecraft image from November 1, 2009. The dramatic illumination reveals the plumes that continuously spew into space from the south pole of Saturn’s 500 kilometer diameter moon . Discovered by Cassini in 2005, the icy plumes are likely connected to an ocean beneath the ice shell of Enceladus.

articles.title: NASA Announces X-70 Experimental Aircraft to Advance Flight Research
articles.excerpt: On Wednesday, NASA unveiled its newest experimental aircraft, the X-70 Fractal, during the UP.Summit at the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. This high-performance, highly adaptable research p…
articles.body: Generated image of NASA’s new X-70 Fractal experimental aircraft, a crewed, rapidly reconfigurable research platform for advanced aviation technologies. On Wednesday, NASA unveiled its newest experimental aircraft, the X-70 Fractal, during the UP.Summit at the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. This high-performance, highly adaptable research platform is designed to accelerate the development and testing of advanced aviation technologies.  The crewed X-70 features advanced, rapidly reconfigurable flight-control technology that will allow NASA to explore aircraft maneuverability in ways never before demonstrated in crewed flight.
